svg.title: Trial design and judgment targets
svg.desc: A shows an illustrative psychology question, an answer B and initial confidence p=80%, generated in one API call and then frozen. B contrasts ordinary reassessment of the answer, yielding q, with a reliability judgment about the original confidence, yielding r=LOW or HIGH. Both review types receive the same full record. An additional fresh call repeats ordinary reassessment to yield q2. Arrows mark the targets of judgment rather than different evidence. C shows the one-review comparison p+r versus p+q and the two-review comparison p+q+r versus p+q+q2. All statistical scorers include subject and are fitted before held-out evaluation. The example is not an observed study response; the metacognitive labels describe tasks, not established mechanisms.
